title: Plots with matplotlib and plotnine
text:
add_basemap() (matplotlib) and geom_basemap() (plotnine) add a basemap under your data. They render when the figure is drawn, for the axes’ extent and at the output resolution: on screen, in this page, or in savefig(dpi=300) and save(dpi=300), labels stay sharp and the right size. Both take the arguments of basemap()’s renderers (labels, features, layers, alpha, …) and credit the provider in the corner.
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", message=".*centroid.*")

import basemapper as bm
import geodatasets
import geopandas as gpd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

nc = gpd.read_file(geodatasets.get_path("geoda.sids"))

title: Plots with matplotlib and plotnine
text:
Projected data
The basemap is rendered in Web Mercator and warped to the axes’ CRS, so data in any CRS works. Here North Carolina’s state plane (EPSG:32119), with the counties’ centroids sized by births:

nc_sp = nc.to_crs(32119)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3.6))
nc_sp.boundary.plot(ax=ax, color="0.15", linewidth=0.3)
nc_sp.centroid.plot(ax=ax, markersize=nc_sp.BIR74 / 300, color="#D96E34", alpha=0.7)
bm.add_basemap(ax, "Esri.WorldTopoMap", crs=nc_sp.crs)
ax.set_axis_off()

title: Plots with matplotlib and plotnine
text:
A quieter basemap
For a data map, a basemap often reads better without its labels, faded, or with only some of its features (see Stacking, labels and features):

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3.6))
nc.assign(share=nc.NWBIR74 / nc.BIR74).plot(
    ax=ax, column="share", cmap="viridis", edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.2, legend=True,
    legend_kwds={"label": "Share of births, non-white, 1974", "shrink": 0.7},
)
bm.add_basemap(ax, "OpenFreeMap.Liberty", labels=False, features=["-roads", "-rail"], alpha=0.6, crs=nc.crs)
ax.set_axis_off()

title: Plots with matplotlib and plotnine
text:
Zooming in
The basemap follows the axes, so setting their limits zooms it in, with detail to match:

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5.2))
nc.boundary.plot(ax=ax, color="yellow", linewidth=1)
for _, row in nc.iterrows():
    p = row.geometry.representative_point()
    if -76.9 < p.x < -75.4 and 35.0 < p.y < 36.0:
        ax.annotate(row.NAME, (p.x, p.y), color="white", fontsize=9, fontweight="bold", ha="center")
ax.set_xlim(-76.9, -75.4)
ax.set_ylim(35.0, 36.0)
bm.add_basemap(ax, "Esri.WorldImagery", crs=nc.crs)
ax.set_axis_off()

title: Plots with matplotlib and plotnine
text:
Credits
The credit line is on by default. attribution=False turns it off; get_attribution() returns the text, for a caption:

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3.6))
nc.boundary.plot(ax=ax, color="steelblue", linewidth=0.4)
bm.add_basemap(ax, "Esri.WorldGrayCanvas", attribution=False, crs=nc.crs)
ax.set_axis_off()
fig.text(0.98, 0.02, bm.get_attribution("Esri.WorldGrayCanvas"), ha="right", fontsize=6, color="0.4")

title: Stacking, labels and features
text:
A style is a stack of layers: background, water, roads, labels and so on. basemapper can draw only some of them, and can stack several styles into one map.

import basemapper as bm

slc = (-111.8887, 40.7556)
def view(style, **kw):
    return bm.basemap(style, 720, 405, center=slc, zoom=12.4, **kw)


What a style draws
list_layers() lists a style’s layers in drawing order, with the vector tile layer each one draws (source_layer) and the feature it shows:

from collections import Counter

layers = bm.list_layers("OpenFreeMap.Liberty")
print(len(layers), "layers")
for l in layers[:10]:
    print(f"{l['id']:<22} {l['type']:<10} {str(l['source_layer']):<14} {l['feature']}")
print(Counter(l["feature"] for l in layers))

111 layers
background             background None           background
natural_earth          raster     None           terrain
park                   fill       park           parks
park_outline           line       park           parks
landuse_residential    fill       landuse        landcover
landcover_wood         fill       landcover      landcover
landcover_grass        fill       landcover      landcover
landcover_ice          fill       landcover      landcover
landcover_wetland      fill       landcover      landcover
landuse_pitch          fill       landuse        landcover
Counter({'roads': 58, 'rail': 12, 'landcover': 11, 'places': 9, 'water': 7, 'poi': 5, 'boundaries': 3, 'parks': 2, 'buildings': 2, 'background': 1, 'terrain': 1})




Labels
labels=False draws a style without its labels (text and icons):

view("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", labels=False)








labels="only" draws just the labels, on a transparent background, to go over another map.


Stacking
A list of styles is drawn bottom to top. To filter one style of a stack, give the filter to basemap_provider(); this puts satellite imagery under a vector basemap’s labels:

hybrid = ["Esri.WorldImagery", bm.basemap_provider("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", labels="only")]
view(hybrid)








ArcGIS basemaps are often published as separate services, drawn in order. The Utah Geospatial Resource Center’s Lite basemap is a hillshade, a base map and labels:

ugrc = "https://tiles.arcgis.com/tiles/99lidPhWCzftIe9K/arcgis/rest/services"
lite = [f"{ugrc}/{s}/VectorTileServer/resources/styles/root.json"
        for s in ["VectorHillshade", "LiteBase", "LiteLabels"]]
bm.basemap(lite, 720, 405, center=(-111.75, 40.62), zoom=10.5)










Features
features keeps or drops parts of the map by what they show: background, water, landcover, parks, buildings, roads, rail, boundaries, places, poi and terrain. Plain names keep, "-name" drops.

view("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", labels=False, features=["background", "water", "parks", "roads"])









view("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", features=["-roads", "-rail", "-poi"])








list_layers() takes the same filters and lists what a render with them draws, to check a filter before rendering:

for l in bm.list_layers("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", labels=False, features=["water", "parks"]):
    print(f"{l['id']:<22} {l['type']:<6} {l['feature']}")

park                   fill   parks
park_outline           line   parks
waterway_tunnel        line   water
waterway_river         line   water
waterway_other         line   water
water                  fill   water




Layers
Features are sorted from each layer’s source layer, as a convenience. For exact control, layers keeps layers by id, or drops them with "-"; * and ? are wildcards:

view("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", layers=["-road_*", "-bridge_*", "-tunnel_*"])








A name that matches no layer warns, so a typo does not go unnoticed:

m = view("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", layers=["-lable_village"])
_ = m.render_array()

D:\GitHub\basemapper\py-basemapper\src\basemapper\_basemap.py:200: UserWarning: layers: "-lable_village" matches no layer




In plots
The plot layers take the same arguments:

import geodatasets
import geopandas as gpd
from plotnine import geom_map, ggplot, theme, theme_void

nc = gpd.read_file(geodatasets.get_path("geoda.sids"))
water = bm.basemap_provider("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", features=["water"], labels=False)

(
    ggplot(nc)
    + bm.geom_basemap(["Esri.WorldShadedRelief", water])
    + geom_map(fill=None, color="#262626", size=0.25)
    + theme_void()
    + theme(figure_size=(8, 3.6))
)

title: Basemap gallery
text:
Every basemap in the catalogue that needs no API key, rendered for the same view of the San Francisco Bay Area. The names work as style anywhere: in basemap(), add_basemap(), geom_basemap() and in R and Rust.

import basemapper as bm

providers = bm.list_providers()
keyless = [p for p in providers if p["api_key_env"] is None]
print(len(keyless), "basemaps")

images = {}
for p in keyless:
    m = bm.basemap(p["name"], 340, 220, center=(-122.25, 37.75), zoom=9)
    images[p["name"]] = m.render_png()

23 basemaps

The vector basemaps (OpenFreeMap, and Esri’s vector styles) are drawn from vector tiles by basemapper’s port of MapLibre GL JS; the raster ones are tile images. Esri’s names have both forms; basemap_provider(name, type="raster") picks the other one.

With an API key
CARTO, Stadia Maps and MapTiler need a free API key, read from the environment variable in api_key_env (or given as api_key= to basemap_provider()):

for p in providers:
    if p["api_key_env"]:
        print(f"{p['name']:<26} {p['api_key_env']}")

text:
Style for an OGC WMS GetMap endpoint, as 256 px tiles in EPSG:3857.


Usage


wms_style(
    url,
    layers,
    styles="",
    version="1.3.0",
    format="image/png",
    transparent=False,
    extra_params=None
)


Parameters


url: str

Base service URL without query parameters.

layers: str

LAYERS parameter.

styles: str = ""

STYLES parameter.

version: str = "1.3.0"

Service version (1.1.x sends SRS, 1.3.0 CRS).

Image MIME type.

title: tile_style()
text:
A style for tile data, with overrides.


Usage


tile_style(
    source,
    type=None,
    tile_size=None,
    scheme=None,
    minzoom=None,
    maxzoom=None,
    attribution=None,
    source_layers=None,
    paint=None,
    auth_token=None
)


source is what you could pass as style directly; use this function to override what is detected, or to get the style JSON to edit:

a tile URL template ({z}/{x}/{y}, {quadkey}, {bbox-epsg-3857}, WMTS {TileMatrix}/{TileRow}/{TileCol});
a TileJSON URL or file;
a PMTiles archive: URL, local path or pmtiles:// URL;
an ArcGIS .../MapServer (raster tiles) or .../VectorTileServer (its published style);
a style URL or file (returned with relative URLs made absolute).

Raster tiles get one raster layer. Vector tiles get a default style drawing every source layer (polygons as translucent fills, lines and outlines, points as circles, a colour per source layer) over a transparent background.


Parameters


source: str

The tile data, as above.

type: Optional[str] = None

"raster" or "vector"; detected when None (from the archive header, the TileJSON, the URL’s extension, or one fetched tile).

tile_size: Optional[int] = None

Raster tile size in px (default 256 for tile URLs and archives).

scheme: Optional[str] = None

"xyz" or "tms" (rows counted from the south).

minzoom: Optional[int] = None

Minimum zoom of the tiles.

maxzoom: Optional[int] = None

Maximum zoom of the tiles (overzoomed beyond).

attribution: Optional[str] = None

Attribution text for the source.

source_layers: Optional[List[str]] = None

Vector tiles: the source layers to draw (default all).

paint: Optional[Dict[str, object]] = None

Vector tiles: paint properties for the generated fill-*, line-* and circle-* layers, e.g. {"fill-color": "#ccc"}. Others are dropped with a warning.

auth_token: Optional[str] = None

Optional access token for the tile service.





Returns


 str

The style JSON.





Raises


 ValidationError

If the type cannot be detected or does not match the data, or source is not found.

title: API Reference
text:
Basemap views

Create a view (basemap()), change it (set_view, set_bounds), read it (get_bounds, get_center, get_zoom, get_size) and render it (render_png, render_svg, render_array). The same functions and arguments exist in R.


basemap()

Create a basemap view.

Basemap

A map view rendered headlessly: one style, or several stacked.




Basemap Methods

Methods for the Basemap class


Basemap.set_view()

Set the centre (longitude, latitude) and/or the MapLibre zoom

Basemap.set_bounds()

Fit the view to bounds (in crs, default EPSG:4326), keeping

Basemap.get_bounds()

The view’s (xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) in EPSG:3857 metres, or in

Basemap.get_center()

(longitude, latitude) of the view centre.

Basemap.get_zoom()

The MapLibre zoom of the view.

Basemap.get_size()

(width, height) of rendered images in device pixels.

Basemap.get_attribution()

The attribution text the view’s styles ask maps to show (see

Basemap.__repr__()



Basemap.render_array()

Render to a (height, width, 4) uint8 RGBA array (device pixels).

Basemap.render_png()

Render a PNG, written to path when given. Returns the PNG bytes.

Basemap.render_svg()

Render an SVG (width x height user units; pixel_ratio




One-shot rendering

Render bounds to an RGBA array in one call.


render_basemap_raw()

Render a basemap for bounds in one call.




Plot integrations

Drop a basemap layer into an existing plot, rendered at the output resolution. geom_basemap takes the same arguments in plotnine and ggplot2 (R).


add_basemap()

Render a basemap beneath existing axes content.

geom_basemap

Render a styled basemap beneath plotnine spatial layers.




Styles

Named basemaps (leaflet-providers names, usable as style), styles for your own tile data, and OGC services. Tile data (tile URLs, TileJSON, PMTiles, ArcGIS services) also works as style directly.


basemap_provider()

A named basemap’s style.

list_providers()

The basemaps :func:basemap_provider knows.

providers

Basemap names for autocompletion: providers.CartoDB.Positron is the

tile_style()

A style for tile data, with overrides.

wms_style()

Style for an OGC WMS GetMap endpoint, as 256 px tiles in EPSG:3857.

wmts_style()

Style for an OGC WMTS GetTile (KVP) endpoint. A RESTful WMTS




Style layers and attribution

A style’s layers with their features, for the layers and features filters, and the attribution text it asks maps to show.


list_layers()

List a style’s layers, or preview a filter.

get_attribution()

The attribution text a style asks maps to show.




Tile cache




tile_cache()

The disk cache for map tiles.




Exceptions




BasemapError

Base exception for all basemapper errors.

ValidationError

Raised for invalid bbox, dimensions, zoom, or layer filter.

StyleError

Raised when a style cannot be fetched or parsed.

NetworkError

Raised when tile or style network requests fail.

title: Basemap.render_svg()
text:
Render an SVG (width x height user units; pixel_ratio


Usage


Basemap.render_svg(
    path=None, text="editable", embed_fonts="subset", font_dirs=None
)


does not apply), written to path when given: vector layers as paths and text, raster tiles (raster basemaps, hillshade) as embedded images. Returns the SVG text.


Parameters


path: Optional[str] = None

Output file, or None.

text: str = "editable"

"editable": labels are <text> elements (editable, selectable) at MapLibre’s glyph positions, halos as strokes, with the style’s fonts embedded; labels whose font file is not available fall back to "bitmap". "bitmap": every label drawn from the style’s own glyph bitmaps, thresholded by SVG filters as MapLibre’s shader does (MapLibre’s look at any zoom; not editable). "paths": glyph outlines traced from those bitmaps (plain paths, no filters).

embed_fonts: str = "subset"

"subset" (only the glyphs used), "full" (whole fonts, for retyping labels) or "none" (fonts by name only). Fonts come from font_dirs, the BASEMAPPER_FONT_DIRS folders, a local cache, then Google Fonts for open fonts; others are referenced by name.

font_dirs: Optional[List[str]] = None

Folders of .ttf / .otf files to use first.

title: basemapper
text:
Installation

Prerequisites
The package compiles a Rust extension during installation. Install Rust for your platform before proceeding.

Windows
winget install Rustlang.Rustup
After installation, open a new terminal so rustup and cargo are on your PATH.


macOS
brew install rustup
rustup-init
Or without Homebrew:
curl https://sh.rustup.rs -sSf | sh


Linux
curl https://sh.rustup.rs -sSf | sh



Install the package
Install the development version from GitHub.
With pip:
pip install "basemapper @ git+https://github.com/ar-puuk/basemapper#subdirectory=py-basemapper"
With uv, into a project or the current environment:
uv add "basemapper @ git+https://github.com/ar-puuk/basemapper#subdirectory=py-basemapper"
uv pip install "basemapper @ git+https://github.com/ar-puuk/basemapper#subdirectory=py-basemapper"
With conda (or mamba), conda-forge provides the dependencies and the Rust toolchain, and pip builds basemapper from GitHub inside the environment:
conda create -n basemapper -c conda-forge python numpy pyproj matplotlib xarray rust pip
conda activate basemapper
pip install "basemapper @ git+https://github.com/ar-puuk/basemapper#subdirectory=py-basemapper"
or as an environment.yml (conda env create -f environment.yml):
name: basemapper
channels: [conda-forge]
dependencies:
  - python>=3.9
  - numpy
  - pyproj
  - matplotlib
  - xarray
  - rust
  - pip
  - pip:
      - "basemapper @ git+https://github.com/ar-puuk/basemapper#subdirectory=py-basemapper"
For geom_basemap() in plotnine, install basemapper[plotnine] in place of basemapper.

A PyPI release is planned once the package stabilises.

title: basemapper
text:
Quick example
import basemapper
from basemapper import basemap_provider, tile_style, wms_style

# Built-in basemaps by leaflet name (list_providers(), basemapper.providers);
# the name works as a style
style = "OpenFreeMap.Liberty"
style = basemap_provider("Esri.WorldGrayCanvas", type="raster")   # pick the form
style = basemap_provider("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", tiles="data/omt.pmtiles")   # your own tiles

# Stack parts of basemaps: imagery under a vector basemap's labels
hybrid = ["Esri.WorldImagery", basemap_provider("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", labels="only")]
# labels=False / "only", features=["water", "roads"] / ["-buildings"]

# A view: centre + zoom, or bounds to fit
m = basemapper.basemap(style, 800, 600, center=(-122.45, 37.75), zoom=12, pixel_ratio=2)
m.render_png(path="sf.png")        # 1600 x 1200
m.render_svg(path="sf.svg")        # true vector
m.set_view(zoom=13).get_bounds(lonlat=True)

# One-shot render of bounds to a (height, width, 4) uint8 array
a = basemapper.render_basemap_raw([-122.5, 37.7, -122.4, 37.8], 400, 300, style)

# Your own tile data works as a style: tile URLs, TileJSON, PMTiles
# archives (URL or local file), ArcGIS services
m = basemapper.basemap("data/area.pmtiles", 800, 600, bounds=[-122.5, 37.7, -122.4, 37.8])
style = tile_style("https://example.com/{z}/{x}/{y}.png", maxzoom=16)   # with overrides
style = wms_style("https://gis.example.com/wms", layers="imagery")

title: add_basemap()
text:
Render a basemap beneath existing axes content.


Usage


add_basemap(
    ax,
    style,
    tile_zoom=None,
    alpha=1.0,
    layers=None,
    labels=True,
    features=None,
    pixel_ratio=None,
    auth_token=None,
    tile_timeout_ms=10000,
    max_tiles=256,
    attribution=True,
    crs=None
)


The basemap is an artist that renders when the figure is drawn, at the output resolution: on screen at the canvas dpi, and natively at the requested resolution in savefig(dpi=...) or PDF / SVG output. Takes the same arguments as :class:geom_basemap (and R’s geom_basemap()).


Parameters


ax: ‘matplotlib.axes.Axes’

An existing matplotlib Axes.

style: Union[str, Any, Sequence[Any]]

A MapLibre GL style URL or JSON string (e.g. from :func:basemap_provider), or a list of those stacked bottom to top.

tile_zoom: Optional[int] = None

Tile detail override: the tile zoom on the 256 px grid (vector sources use one less), or None to pick tiles as MapLibre does for the view.

alpha: float = 1.0

Opacity of the basemap layer (0.0–1.0).

layers: Optional[List[str]] = None

Optional layer filter. Plain IDs keep only those layers; minus-prefixed IDs drop those layers; * and ? are wildcards.

labels: Union[bool, str] = True

True keeps every layer, False drops the labels (text and icons), "only" keeps only the labels on a transparent background, to stack over another map. Catalogue raster basemaps switch to their label-free or label-only tiles.

features: Optional[List[str]] = None

Optional feature filter applied to every style: plain names keep those features, - prefixed names drop them, e.g. ["water", "roads"] or ["-buildings"]. Features: background, water, landcover, parks, buildings, roads, rail, boundaries, places, poi, terrain, other (see the feature of :func:list_layers).

pixel_ratio: Optional[float] = None

Device pixels per CSS pixel (MapLibre’s devicePixelRatio). Default: output dpi / 96, so lines and labels keep their physical size at any dpi. Larger values draw map symbols smaller.

auth_token: Optional[str] = None

Optional access token for the tile service.

tile_timeout_ms: int = 10000

Per-tile HTTP timeout in milliseconds.

max_tiles: int = 256

Maximum tile downloads per style.

attribution: Union[bool, str] = True

The credit line the basemap’s providers ask for, drawn small in the bottom-right corner over the plot: True (the default) for the styles’ own (see :func:get_attribution), False for none, or your own text.

crs: Optional[object] = None

CRS of the axes data coordinates (anything pyproj.CRS accepts, e.g. "EPSG:4326", gdf.crs). Required for plain matplotlib axes and GeoDataFrame plots, whose axes carry no CRS; detected automatically for cartopy axes when omitted.





Returns


 ‘xr.DataArray’

xarray.DataArray of shape (height, width, 4) holding the first render
(at the figure’s current dpi), with spatial bounds and CRS in
.attrs. The live artist is ax.images[-1].





Raises


 BasemapError

If CRS detection fails, the render fails, or the network is unreachable.

title: basemap_provider()
text:
A named basemap’s style.


Usage


basemap_provider(
    name, type=None, api_key=None, tiles=None, labels=True, features=None
)


Names follow leaflet-providers ("CartoDB.Positron", "Esri.WorldImagery", "OpenStreetMap.HOT"); see :func:list_providers or the :data:providers object. A name also works as style directly; this function picks the form, passes a key, or swaps in your own tiles.


Parameters


name: str

Basemap name (case-insensitive).

type: Optional[str] = None

"vector" (a MapLibre style) or "raster" (tiles). By default the vector form when there is one, else raster. Asking for a form a basemap lacks is an error, never a silent fallback.

api_key: Optional[str] = None

API key for CARTO, MapTiler and Stadia; by default read from CARTO_API_KEY, MAPTILER_API_KEY or STADIA_API_KEY. The keys are free for moderate use; :func:list_providers shows which basemaps need one.

tiles: Optional[str] = None

Your own tile data to draw with this basemap’s style: a .pmtiles archive (URL or path), tile URL or TileJSON. It must use the same schema as the provider’s tiles (OpenMapTiles for OpenFreeMap and Stadia).

labels: Union[bool, str] = True

True keeps every layer, False drops the labels, "only" keeps only the labels, to stack this basemap’s labels over another map. Raster tiles switch to the provider’s label-free or label-only tiles (an error when it has none).

features: Optional[List[str]] = None

Vector form: features to keep (["water", "roads"]) or drop (["-buildings"]); see :func:list_layers.





Returns


 str

A style URL, or inline style JSON (the raster form, or with
tiles, labels or features).





Raises


 ValidationError

For an unknown name (with suggestions), a form the basemap lacks, or a missing API key.

title: get_attribution()
text:
The attribution text a style asks maps to show.


Usage


get_attribution(style, auth_token=None)


Every source the style’s layers draw from contributes its attribution (from the style, the source’s TileJSON or PMTiles metadata), as MapLibre’s attribution control collects it, as plain text without duplicates, joined with " | ". Use it for a caption or a credit line, e.g. ax.annotate(get_attribution(style), ...). :meth:Basemap.get_attribution gives a view’s. The same function exists in R (get_attribution()).


Parameters


style: Any

A style (anything :func:basemap takes), or a list of styles stacked bottom to top.

auth_token: Optional[str] = None

Optional access token for the tile service.





Returns


 str

The attribution; an empty string when the styles give none.

title: list_layers()
text:
List a style’s layers, or preview a filter.


Usage


list_layers(style, auth_token=None, layers=None, labels=True, features=None)


The layers of a style in drawing order: their id (what layers matches), type (symbol layers are the labels labels keeps or drops), source_layer (the vector tile layer drawn, None for background and raster layers) and feature (what features matches). With layers, labels or features, the layers a render with those filters draws; an empty list when they leave nothing. The same function exists in R (list_layers(), returning a data frame).
A layer’s feature comes from its source layer, with tables for the OpenMapTiles (OpenFreeMap, Stadia, MapTiler), Protomaps (CARTO) and Shortbread (VersaTiles) schemas, and keywords for others (Esri’s descriptive names, layer ids). It is a convenience: check it here, and use layers for exact control.


Parameters


style: Any

A style (anything :func:basemap takes).

auth_token: Optional[str] = None

Optional access token for the style URL.

layers: Optional[List[str]] = None

Layer filter to preview: plain IDs keep, - prefixed IDs drop; * and ? are wildcards.

labels: Union[bool, str] = True

True, False or "only", as the renderers take it.

features: Optional[List[str]] = None

Feature filter to preview, as the renderers take it.





Returns


 List[Dict[str, Optional[str]]]

A list of {"id", "type", "source_layer", "feature"} dicts
(pandas.DataFrame(...) turns it into a table).





Raises


 BasemapError

If the style cannot be fetched or parsed, or a filter is invalid.

title: render_basemap_raw()
text:
Render a basemap for bounds in one call.


Usage


render_basemap_raw(
    bounds,
    width,
    height,
    style,
    crs=None,
    pixel_ratio=1.0,
    tile_zoom=None,
    layers=None,
    labels=True,
    features=None,
    auth_token=None,
    tile_timeout_ms=10000,
    max_tiles=256,
    tile_concurrency=16,
    fail_on_tile_error=False
)


A one-shot render: fit bounds into a width x height CSS-pixel view and return the pixels. :func:basemap with :meth:Basemap.render_array gives the same result with a reusable view. The same function exists in R (render_basemap_raw()).


Parameters


bounds: Any

Bounding box: a [xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax] sequence in crs (default EPSG:4326, with a warning when the values look projected), a dict with xmin/ymin/xmax/ymax (and optionally crs) keys, or a GeoDataFrame / GeoSeries (CRS read from it).

width: int

View width in CSS pixels.

height: int

View height in CSS pixels.

style: Any

A MapLibre GL style URL or JSON string (e.g. from :func:basemap_provider), or a list of those stacked bottom to top.

crs: Optional[Any] = None

CRS of bounds (anything pyproj.CRS accepts).

pixel_ratio: float = 1.0

Device pixels per CSS pixel; the image is width * pixel_ratio by height * pixel_ratio.

tile_zoom: Optional[int] = None

Tile detail override: the tile zoom on the 256 px grid (vector sources use one less, their tiles being 512 px), or None to pick tiles as MapLibre does for the view.

layers: Optional[List[str]] = None

Optional layer filter: plain IDs keep only those layers, - prefixed IDs drop them; * and ? are wildcards ("-label_*").

labels: Union[bool, str] = True

True keeps every layer, False drops the labels (text and icons), "only" keeps only the labels on a transparent background, to stack over another map. Catalogue raster basemaps switch to their label-free or label-only tiles.

features: Optional[List[str]] = None

Optional feature filter applied to every style: plain names keep those features, - prefixed names drop them, e.g. ["water", "roads"] or ["-buildings"]. Features: background, water, landcover, parks, buildings, roads, rail, boundaries, places, poi, terrain, other (see the feature of :func:list_layers).

auth_token: Optional[str] = None

Optional access token for the tile service.

tile_timeout_ms: int = 10000

Per-tile HTTP timeout in milliseconds.

max_tiles: int = 256

Maximum tiles fetched per style.

tile_concurrency: int = 16

Parallel tile downloads.

fail_on_tile_error: bool = False

Abort on a failed tile instead of leaving it empty.





Returns


 np.ndarray

numpy.ndarray: (height * pixel_ratio, width * pixel_ratio, 4)
uint8 RGBA pixels.





Raises


 BasemapError

On any rendering or network failure.

title: tile_cache()

The disk cache for map tiles.

Tiles are kept as long as the server’s caching headers allow (a day when they say nothing), so repeated renders of an area do not download them again. The cache starts in BASEMAPPER_CACHE_DIR when set (off disables it), else in the platform cache directory.


Parameters


dir: Optional[str] = None

Move the cache to this directory; False or "" turns it off. None leaves it as it is.

clear: bool = False

Delete every cached tile.





Returns


 Optional[str]

The cache directory, or None when the cache is off.

title: Get started
text:
R or Rust? The same functions and arguments exist in R (verb(m, ...) for Python’s m.verb(...)) and Rust.

basemapper renders MapLibre GL basemaps headlessly with a Rust core: no browser, display server, GPU or GDAL. Vector styles are drawn by a software port of MapLibre GL JS’s renderer, so maps look as they do in MapLibre. Everything on this page was run when the page was built; the maps are the output of the code above them.

Installation
pip install "basemapper @ git+https://github.com/ar-puuk/basemapper#subdirectory=py-basemapper"
# or: uv add "basemapper @ git+https://github.com/ar-puuk/basemapper#subdirectory=py-basemapper"
See the home page for conda.


Choose a style
Every function takes a style. The simplest is a named basemap, a leaflet-providers name; list_providers() lists them, with the API key some need:

import basemapper as bm

for p in bm.list_providers()[:12]:
    print(f"{p['name']:<24} vector={p['vector']!s:<5} raster={p['raster']!s:<5} key={p['api_key_env']}")

OpenStreetMap.Mapnik     vector=False raster=True  key=None
OpenStreetMap.DE         vector=False raster=True  key=None
OpenStreetMap.France     vector=False raster=True  key=None
OpenStreetMap.HOT        vector=False raster=True  key=None
OpenTopoMap              vector=False raster=True  key=None
CyclOSM                  vector=False raster=True  key=None
OpenFreeMap.Liberty      vector=True  raster=False key=None
OpenFreeMap.Bright       vector=True  raster=False key=None
OpenFreeMap.Positron     vector=True  raster=False key=None
OpenFreeMap.Dark         vector=True  raster=False key=None
OpenFreeMap.Fiord        vector=True  raster=False key=None
CartoDB.Positron         vector=True  raster=True  key=CARTO_API_KEY


A MapLibre style URL or JSON works too, and so does tile data: a tile URL, TileJSON, PMTiles archive or ArcGIS service (see Your own tiles and services).


A map on its own
basemap() creates a view: a centre and MapLibre zoom (or bounds to fit), and a size in CSS pixels. In a notebook, a view shows the map:

m = bm.basemap("OpenFreeMap.Positron", 720, 405, center=(-111.8887, 40.7556), zoom=12.4)
m








repr() describes it, and the get_*() methods read it:

print(repr(m))
print(m.get_bounds(lonlat=True))
print(m.get_attribution())

<Basemap 1 style, 720 x 405 @ 1x (720 x 405 px), center (-111.88870, 40.75560), zoom 12.400>
(-111.93553419871802, 40.73564121457685, -111.841865801282, 40.77555279531684)
OpenFreeMap © OpenMapTiles Data from OpenStreetMap


set_view() and set_bounds() change the view. Here it fits North Carolina’s counties (a GeoDataFrame, from geodatasets):

import geopandas as gpd
import geodatasets

nc = gpd.read_file(geodatasets.get_path("geoda.sids"))
bm.basemap("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", 720, 300, bounds=nc)










Raster and vector, PNG and SVG
Basemaps come as raster tiles (images, like OpenStreetMap’s) or vector tiles (geometry styled on the fly, like OpenFreeMap’s). Either renders to a PNG with render_png() or an SVG with render_svg(). In an SVG, vector layers are paths and the labels editable text with the style’s fonts embedded; raster tiles are embedded as images.

import os, tempfile

slc = (-111.8910, 40.7608)
raster = bm.basemap("OpenStreetMap.Mapnik", 480, 300, center=slc, zoom=11.5)
vector = bm.basemap("OpenFreeMap.Bright", 480, 300, center=slc, zoom=11.5)

out = tempfile.mkdtemp()
for name, m in [("raster", raster), ("vector", vector)]:
    m.render_png(os.path.join(out, f"{name}.png"))
    m.render_svg(os.path.join(out, f"{name}.svg"))

for f in sorted(os.listdir(out)):
    print(f"{f:<12} {os.path.getsize(os.path.join(out, f)) // 1024} KB")

raster.png   228 KB
raster.svg   305 KB
vector.png   81 KB
vector.svg   429 KB




PNGSVG
RasterOpenStreetMap
VectorOpenFreeMap Bright


render_array() returns the pixels, for your own compositing, and get_bounds() their extent in Web Mercator:

a = vector.render_array()
a.shape, a.dtype, vector.get_bounds()

((300, 480, 4),
 dtype('uint8'),
 (-12462135.04127428,
  4973069.79762207,
  -12449163.247426074,
  4981177.168777199))


pixel_ratio makes images larger with the same view and label layout: pixel_ratio=2 for a sharp 2x image, dpi / 96 for print.


In a plot
add_basemap() adds a basemap under a matplotlib axes’ content. It renders when the figure is drawn, for the axes’ extent and at the output resolution, and credits the provider in the corner:

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

nc_3857 = nc.to_crs(3857)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3.6))
nc_3857.plot(ax=ax, column="BIR74", cmap="viridis", alpha=0.75, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.3, legend=True)
bm.add_basemap(ax, "OpenFreeMap.Positron", crs=3857)
ax.set_axis_off()








geom_basemap() does the same in plotnine, with the arguments of R’s geom_basemap():

from plotnine import aes, geom_map, ggplot, scale_fill_cmap, theme_void, theme

(
    ggplot(nc)
    + bm.geom_basemap("Esri.WorldGrayCanvas")
    + geom_map(aes(fill="SID74"), alpha=0.7, color="white", size=0.2)
    + scale_fill_cmap("Blues", name="SIDS, 1974")
    + theme_void()
    + theme(figure_size=(8, 3.6))
)








Plots with matplotlib and plotnine has more.

title: Your own tiles and services
text:
Besides named basemaps and MapLibre styles, style takes tile data: a tile URL template, TileJSON, a PMTiles archive (URL or local file), or an ArcGIS service. basemapper detects whether the tiles are raster or vector and builds a style for them; tile_style() builds one with your overrides. OGC services (WMS, WMTS) have their own style builders.
import basemapper as bm

title: Your own tiles and services
text:
With a basemap style
A vector archive can also be drawn with a full basemap style whose source points at it. protomaps-light.json and protomaps-dark.json are the Protomaps basemap styles with the Florence archive as their source ("url": "pmtiles://https://pmtiles.io/protomaps(vector)ODbL_firenze.pmtiles"), and a style file’s path works as style:

bm.basemap("styles/protomaps-light.json", 720, 405, center=(11.2551, 43.7710), zoom=15.2)









bm.basemap("styles/protomaps-dark.json", 720, 405, center=(11.2551, 43.7710), zoom=15.2)








For your own Protomaps archive, change the source’s url to pmtiles:// and the archive’s URL or path. These styles are for Protomaps tiles v3; archives built from late 2024 on use tiles v4, with the styles of @protomaps/basemaps 5 (how the styles were made).
